title: Delegate pay is conditioned on explanation quality that the Atlas admits it has no criteria to assess
content:
A.1.6.4.3.2 mirrors the voting-activity gradient for communications: falling below 95% of eligible votes explained reduces the Ranked Delegate's budget stream by 5% per point, and at 75% the income stops entirely. The annotation A.1.6.4.3.2.0.3.2 states the purpose — "to ensure that SKY holders delegating to the AD have full transparency to understand the AD's decision-making process" — and locates the artefact: explanations "are posted in the AD's Forum thread."

NR-12 then asks the question the metric depends on and cannot answer: "should there be explicit criteria for Aligned Delegates' voting-communications? What constitutes an adequate explanation for each vote? How would the Core Facilitator evaluate ADs' explanations for quality, completeness, etc.? How can the Core Facilitator objectively assess explanations that may vary widely in style and content?"

The gap is consequential because the metric is *binary per vote* — an explanation either counts or it does not — while the underlying quality is continuous and unspecified. A.1.6.2.2 supplies three content tests (demonstrated understanding of core mechanisms, a reasoned basis, engagement with a substantive aspect), but nothing maps those onto a compliant/non-compliant determination, and money turns on that determination monthly.

NR-12 names the failure mode precisely: without criteria there is "the potential failure of the Target Document's objective to ensure that ADs' voting activity is transparent to SKY holders who have delegated to that AD." A metric satisfiable by minimal text measures posting frequency, not transparency — and a delegate optimizing against an unspecified standard rationally produces the shortest thing that has historically been accepted.

NR-12 also flags an unaddressed dimension: "Should more complex or high-stakes votes require more detailed explanations than routine or procedural votes?" As written, every vote counts equally, so effort is best spent uniformly rather than where the stakes are.
description: A.1.6.4.3.2 applies the same 95%-to-75% budget gradient to vote explanations, while NR-12 concedes there are no explicit adequacy criteria and names the resulting transparency risk.
